content: The Expo anticipates an extraordinary 193 billion USD worth of investments, indicative of longstanding, targeted efforts to mobilize private sector funding to bridge the infrastructure deficit [33] . For the competitive crane hire industry, these trends dictate a strategic imperative to modernize fleets, ensuring the availability of versatile, high-capacity lifting equipment capable of servicing both specialized renewable energy installations and heavy civil engineering projects. Energy Sector Expansion and Renewable Installations The South African energy sector underwent notable developments between 2020 and 2024, characterized by concerted efforts to address the nation’s historical reliance on coal and to strategically diversify its energy mix. Throughout this period, coal remained the dominant energy source, accounting for approximately 70 percent of installed power generation capacity, a persistent trend driven by abundant local availability and the extensive historical infrastructure built to support it . While strategic plans were firmly in place during these earlier years, subsequent post-2024 analyses revealed that numerous projects suffered from extended timelines and required enhanced policy coherence, which ultimately impeded immediate implementation and the realization of associated economic benefits [41] [42] . Progress in reducing the share of fossil fuels in the national energy portfolio was neither rapid nor extensive enough to completely transform the sector during this timeframe [43] . However, private-sector participation began to bridge the gap. Private Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) increasingly contributed to the growth of the renewable sector, with solar, wind, and energy storage initiatives playing leading roles and reflecting the private sector's proactive engagement in securing reliable power [10] . A notable historical example of this private-sector momentum is the March 2022 launch of Envusa Energy’s Koruson 2 initiative, a strategic joint venture between Anglo American and EDF Renewables aimed at achieving ambitious clean energy targets by 2030 [45] . The Western Cape has strategically emerged as a focal point for renewable energy developments, bolstered by favorable regional policies and investment incentives that signal substantial future growth potential . International support has also played a pivotal role in facilitating this transition.
